questions.stem: An interactive assistant may process requests across EU countries but cannot process them outside the EU. Usage varies, and the team wants token-based billing. The model supports all listed types. Which deployment fits?

options.text: Data Zone Standard, using EU capacity with token-based charges for interactive requests.
Global Standard in an EU resource, relying on the resource region to keep inference processing within the EU.
Data Zone Batch, submitting requests to the asynchronous batch queue.
Data Zone Provisioned, with EU processing and reserved throughput.

explanation.whyCorrect: Data Zone Standard combines the EU processing boundary with on-demand token billing. Model availability and quota must also be available in the selected deployment.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: Global processing is not restricted to the EU by the resource location.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: The workload calls for usage-based billing rather than reserved throughput.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: The assistant needs responses during the user interaction.

questions.stem: A service has predictable sustained model traffic and needs allocated throughput. Its processing boundary is already satisfied by the chosen region. Which deployment characteristic should drive the selection?

options.text: Developer deployment for experimentation with the selected model.
Batch processing with deferred completion for groups of requests.
Standard token billing with capacity shared across on-demand requests.
Provisioned capacity with a throughput commitment.

explanation.whyCorrect: Provisioned deployments allocate throughput under a capacity commitment. Size the commitment using measured workload characteristics rather than equating it with on-demand quota.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: This does not reserve the planned throughput.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Deferred completion does not meet a sustained interactive serving need.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: An experimentation deployment does not meet the production capacity requirement.

questions.stem: Developers have scoped Foundry RBAC roles, but a shared resource key authenticates the application. A developer can perform an operation that their role excludes. Which change makes the role assignments effective for those calls?

options.text: Move the application behind a private endpoint while retaining key authentication.
Rotate the shared resource key and continue assigning each developer the same key.
Store the shared key in a vault and distribute it to authorized developers.
Authenticate with Entra identities carrying the intended scoped roles.

explanation.whyCorrect: Foundry RBAC applies to Microsoft Entra authentication. A resource key grants access outside those individual role restrictions.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: Rotation does not make a shared key enforce individual RBAC.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: Network isolation does not change the authorization semantics of the key.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: Protecting storage does not apply user-role restrictions to key-authenticated calls.

questions.stem: A secured agent has the required runtime roles. Search resolves to a public IP from the agent network even though public access is disabled. The private endpoint exists. What should be investigated next?

options.text: Private DNS resolution and links for the agent network.
The query-time semantic ranking configuration on the target index.
The private endpoint connection approval state for the runtime subnet.
The Search role assignments on the identity used by the deployment pipeline.

explanation.whyCorrect: A private endpoint must be reachable through correct DNS resolution and routing from the runtime network. Roles cannot repair resolution to a blocked public endpoint.

whyDistractorsWrong.C: The stated failure is name resolution to a public address.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: The problem is name resolution from the runtime network.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Ranking is evaluated after a request reaches Search.

questions.stem: A Foundry managed-compute preview deployment needs more accelerators. Matching GPU VM quota is available in the same region. Which quota should the team request?

options.text: Request a larger subscription-wide regional vCPU allocation and count that capacity toward the Foundry managed-compute accelerator deployment.
An increase to the classic managed-endpoint GPU VM-family quota for that region.
Request the regional accelerator-SKU allocation through the Foundry managed-compute quota process.
Additional tokens per minute on the serverless language model deployment.

explanation.whyCorrect: Managed-compute preview uses its own quota per accelerator SKU and region. Existing Azure VM quota cannot be applied to it.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: Classic VM quota is a separate allocation.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Token quota does not allocate managed-compute accelerators.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: Foundry managed-compute quota is separate from the subscription VM allocation.

questions.stem: A hosted agent returns session_quota_exceeded. Several sessions no longer need active compute, but their stored state is still required. What should the operator do?

options.text: Stop the inactive sessions that are consuming active capacity.
Delete the completed sessions together with their stored conversation state.
Increase the model deployment’s reserved inference throughput.
Increase the tokens-per-minute allocation for the underlying chat model.

explanation.whyCorrect: Stopping sessions that no longer need active compute releases active session capacity while respecting the requirement to retain state.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: The requirement explicitly preserves the state.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: The reported code concerns sessions, not model tokens.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: Model throughput is separate from active hosted-session capacity.

questions.stem: A GitHub workflow must deploy a hosted agent with no long-lived Azure credential stored in GitHub. Which identity setup fits the documented deployment pattern?

options.text: A client-secret credential copied into GitHub and rotated before each release.
A project endpoint variable used as the workflow's authentication credential.
Federated OIDC authentication with a scoped deployment identity.
The runtime agent identity inferred from the agent name in the workflow file.

explanation.whyCorrect: OIDC federation lets the workflow obtain tokens through a configured trust relationship. The workflow identity still needs the required deployment roles.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: This still stores a long-lived secret credential.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: A name does not establish workflow federation or deployment permissions.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: The endpoint identifies the service; it does not authenticate the workflow.

questions.stem: An agent request traverses retrieval, generation and a business tool. Engineers need to attribute a latency increase to one operation and its parent request. Which telemetry structure supports that?

options.text: Timed service events whose correlation key is the service name shared by all requests.
Record a structured event for each request containing final text, total elapsed time and the names of every participating service.
Export a correlated request trace with timed nested spans for retrieval, generation and the tool call.
Independent traces for each operation, each with a newly generated request identifier.

explanation.whyCorrect: Nested spans represent timed operations inside a request trace. Consistent attributes and parent relationships make the slow stage visible.

whyDistractorsWrong.B: Aggregate request timing and service names do not identify timed nested operations.
whyDistractorsWrong.A: A service name does not connect operations for a particular request.
whyDistractorsWrong.D: Separate identifiers break the shared request hierarchy.

questions.domainName: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution

questions.stem: Tool arguments include account numbers and an access token. Engineers need useful traces for incident diagnosis. Which collection policy best fits?

options.text: Export full content spans to a restricted workspace, then delete secrets in a nightly job.
Store raw access tokens in encrypted span attributes accessible to incident responders.
Remove the request and evaluation identifiers while preserving raw tool arguments.
Redact sensitive fields before export and preserve safe correlation data.

explanation.whyCorrect: Remove credentials and redact personal data before they enter telemetry. Safe identifiers, timings, access controls and retention policies preserve diagnostic value.

whyDistractorsWrong.A: Secrets enter telemetry before the deletion job.
whyDistractorsWrong.C: This loses correlation and retains sensitive content.
whyDistractorsWrong.B: Credentials should not be recorded in telemetry.
